payload.comment:
Preprocessing stage is structurally sound and internally consistent. All arithmetic verifications pass: class counts sum exactly to official split sizes (train 89996, val 10004, test 7180); augmented train size 359984 = 89996×4 is correct; proportions, imbalance ratios (train 1.63, test 3.95), and test-to-train prevalence ratios are arithmetically consistent. No duplicates, no blank images, 100% profiled, all three index SHA-256 hashes and the archive MD5 are present and cross-referenced between the dataset manifest and split manifest. The representation plan (z-score standardization using train-only stats, hflip/vflip/rotate90 augmentation) is appropriate for 28×28 H&E patches and prevents data leakage. The run manifest pins code SHA-256, package versions, seed, and deterministic-torch flag.

Carried-forward warnings (none are blockers for preprocessing):
1. llm_model_digest is null while qwen3.8 via ollama is declared; exact weights are unpinned, limiting full reproducibility of any LLM-dependent annotation or review step. This should be resolved before any LLM-assisted downstream stage.
2. Model name 'qwen3.8' is atypical for the Qwen naming convention (expected patterns: qwen2.5, qwen3, qwen3-8b, etc.); verify it maps to the intended ollama registry checkpoint.
3. Test set (CRC-VAL-HE-7K) originates from a different clinical center with a substantially shifted class distribution (adipose ×1.79, debris ×0.41, stroma ×0.56 relative to train). This is properly documented in the dataset manifest and data profile. Downstream evaluation must report in-domain (train/val) and cross-domain (test) metrics separately.
4. Small per-class test counts (debris n=339, stroma n=421, smooth muscle n=592) will make per-class test metrics statistically noisy; confidence intervals or bootstrap estimates are advisable.
5. Label ambiguity at 28×28 resolution (debris/mucus/background overlap; stroma vs smooth muscle; normal mucosa vs adenocarcinoma epithelium) is well-documented and should inform interpretation of per-class error analysis.
6. No inter-annotator-agreement data for the external center; label semantics for ambiguous classes may differ across sites.

None of these warnings indicate a defect in the preprocessing pipeline itself. The data is correctly ingested, profiled, and the representation plan is sound. Proceed to the next stage with the above warnings tracked for downstream reporting.
